Aviso que si quieren una buena review vayan a ver la que hice de la odisea, voy a defenestrar esta pelicula No sufría TANTO con el acento de una película desde Emilia Pérez. Al pacino todo bien pero que poronga fue eso, casi no usaron actores latinos y la verdad que fue espantoso bancarme esos asentos por casi 3 horas. Que pelicula de mierda, y es que no encuentro más palabras para decirlo. Yo entiendo que siempre hay trabajo detrás de las películas y que siempre hay alguien que se desveló esciribiendo el guion, editándola, asegurándose de que la fotografía esté bien , pero en mi opinión es una mierda. ¿Enserio hay gente que idolatra a Tony Montana? La pelicula quiere hacer una historia de un personaje complejo y duro cuando lo único que hace es decir fuck todo el tiempo. Me pareció un discurso vacío y sin sentido con personajes que carecen de profundidad, siento que se podría haber explorado más y no reducir todo a hacer plata y matar gente. No hay un arco de personaje que logre involucrarte en la historia y solamente grita todo el tiempo para hacernos creer que es un gran personaje y que haya GENTE QUE LO IDOLATRE . WTF. I wanted to see if my opinion had changed at all. It hasn’t. I don’t particularly like Tony’s character. I understand that he isn’t supposed to be a good person, and I appreciate other pieces of media that center around morally bad or complex characters. I enjoyed Breaking Bad and American Psycho. With Tony, however, I feel like he’s simply a stupid person, which makes his psychotic nature more frustrating and, to me, much less nuanced. The one redeeming quality I can give him is that he didn’t want to kill the two kids. Other than that, I just think he’s a genuinely terrible and unintelligent person. The only reason he gained power in the first place was by screwing over the other gangs, and I never felt like he was truly the untouchable drug kingpin the movie seemed to portray him as. From the beginning, he had the cops after him and constantly had people coming after him. Yes, he made a lot of money, but it didn’t last very long. In the end, it felt short lived. His downfall always felt inevitable. Overall, I understand the cultural importance of this movie, and there are definitely a few scenes that I really enjoyed. But even after another rewatch, I still found myself thinking why did this movie have to be three hours long? Lol. Everyone in highschool and college was obsessed with this movie, which I can understand if I was a teenager when it came out. Not a teenager 25-30 years later.  I remember going to friends houses and you would see the iconic movie poster on the wall, or a frame of him at the end of the movie. Quoting it constantly. Maybe it was the first "adult" movie they got to watch because their parents grew up with it, maybe it was their first exposure to hot women with their boobs out, the gangster life style, or the word "fuck" that wasn't said by their father to them.  It is interesting to me that so many men make this movie their whole entire personality, and if you are one of those people, you need help! I obviously never watched this movie as a child, or a teen. Chances are my parent's wouldn't have allowed me to. Then when I was old enough to seek it out, I just didn't care to. My only other exposure to the Scarface franchise besides what was said above was actually the video game for the Nintendo Wii. Why did I own this game at 12, I don't know but I did. I used to have to use the stupid joy con to drive around the little shitty cars in it. I never beat it, it was an open world GTA clone which is funny because Vice City is obviously a clone or heavily inspired by this film. I likely beat the first couple of missions and then drove around killing people. Anyways onto the actual film. A rags to riches to self destruction movie. Obviously a hugely influential movie, for all kinds of future work. I liked it for what it was but I felt that it did drag from time to time. I think from the 3rd act on the movie is extremely good. It really kicks into gear from the wedding on. Obviously the movie is most remembered from the epic conclusion which does live up to the hype. Al/Tony really carries this movie, I did find the movie kind of hokey and Al's over the top acting in majority of the stuff he does really fits the vibes of the movie. I am glad I watched it to finally say that I have but I don't see myself ever choosing to watch it again, and if I have kids someday this wouldn't be the top of the list of movies to show them. ***Revisit to see if my feelings on Scarface have changed as my movie tastes have matured and aged. I was very impressed with how well Carlito's Way was shot and how well each scene seemed to flow into the next. I've seen Scarface maybe three times, and while it's a perfectly fine movie, I had always thought it was overrated. This watch is too see if my more nuanced appreciation for cinematography and certain filmmaking styles will make me appreciate this film more. Relationship between Tony and Elvira seems off to me. Scarface is a fun ride, and I enjoy the ride, but I like I find more flaws in the journey. The editing is poor. The performances and connectivity between a lot of the actors feels off. Scarface is a good movie, with many memorable sequences, but it's less a sum of all parts movie and more individual stand-outs, like the cinematography. I love the feel of this Miami ride, and while shots aren't necessarily sewn together as I prefer, the shots themselves are vibrant, colorful, and full of style. I see why so many rappers and rogues love this movie so much. Scarface is a gangster who doesn't take shit from anyone, gets what he wants, and takes what he wants. This movie is more 'trash gangster' than 'Prestige gangster', which I feel I under appreciated as a genre. The movie hits a different tone 2/3 of the way through the movie when Tony reaches his apex. The film becomes more fun and announces itself with the 'Push It' montage. I don't love the script. I'm not the biggest Oliver Stone fan, and I don't know how much of the script De Palma changed, but certain plot lines just don't quite work for me. While he has his moments, of the elite Al Pacino performances, this is lower on my list. I prefer the cocaine mania of Ray Liotta in Goodfellas to the psychopath Al Pacino cocaine acting. He was absolutely awesome when snorting the comically large mounds of coke. The Gina plot isn't hammy enough to be enjoyed for pure trash, but it isn't well written enough to get any points from a prestige drama. Scarface is definitely elite trash crime, but I prefer Carlito's Way. I do have a much greater appreciation for Scarface for what it is as opposed to what it isn't. 84/100

Given how despicable Tony Montana is, I wasn't expecting to enjoy this as much as I did; but I found myself captivated by Montana's escape from being caged by Cuba's communism, only to run into the tiger's mouth of American capitalism, dragging others with him to be eaten. The movie is excessive, violent, grotesque, dehumanizing because it's the culture these characters live in. Only wealth and status matter to Tony. He wants Elvira as a wife for status. He wants kids for legacy. He wants it all just to prove he can. It's ambition without end. I understand the criticism of Tony's character being empty, but I actually prefer this than trying to portray someone who's abhorrent as "interesting" or "sympathetic". Tony is a scumbag that just gets scummier. There's no pretense about it. He's not naive, nor an innocent in over his head. He asked for it. And he got what he asked for. It's suitably nihilistic. I also think the movie has an immaculate style. I sometimes find De Palma's direction visualy indulgent, but not here. The staging, cinematography, wardrobe, soundtrack, are all superb. Not to mention the performances, highlighted by Pacino. Amongst American gangster films, Scarface does stand apart. It's a great film about a man who wants greatness, but doesn't understand what it means to be great.
